anzsic_codes.name: Waste Remediation and Materials Recovery Services

merger_description:
ReDirect Holdings Pty Limited (**ReDirect**) proposes to acquire 100% of the shares in Echo Solve Pty Limited (**Echo Solve**), including Echo Solve’s contaminated waste treatment facility business (the **Acquisition**).

ReDirect is a resource recovery and recycling business operating principally in New South Wales. Its activities include collecting, processing, and recycling waste materials (including wood, metal and drill mud) that would otherwise be landfill, and producing recycled materials for re-use.

As part of ReDirect’s drill mud arm of the business, it owns and operates a drill mud facility located in Wetherill Park, New South Wales (**Wetherill Park Drill Mud Recycling**).

Echo Solve has a contaminated waste treatment facility located and operating principally in Altona, Victoria (the **Altona Thermal Desorption Plant**). It conducts contaminated soil treatment operations via thermal desorption, drill mud disposal, hydro-excavation and soil washing.

Echo Solve is owned by Next Capital and other former Enviropacific Services Pty Limited shareholders/management.

On completion of the Acquisition, ReDirect will acquire 100% of the shares in Echo Solve, and the associated assets and liabilities. This includes:

* Echo Solve’s contaminated waste treatment facility business;
* the Lease Agreement between Echo Solve and the current landlord of the Altona Thermal Desorption Plant; and
* all Employee and business contracts entered into by Echo Solve.

determination_table_content.details:
ReDirect Holdings Pty Limited (ReDirect) applied for a notification
waiver in respect of its proposed acquisition of 100% of the share
capital in Echo Solve Pty Limited (Echo Solve), including Echo
Solve’s contaminated waste treatment facility business, as
described in the transaction documents provided as part of the
application (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

The acquirer, ReDirect, is a resource recovery and recycling business
operating principally in New South Wales. Its activities include
collecting, processing, and recycling waste materials (including
wood, metal and drill mud) that would otherwise be landfill, and
producing recycled materials for re-use. As part of ReDirect’s drill
mud arm of the business, it owns and operates a drill mud facility
located in Wetherill Park, New South Wales. ReDirect also has a
small liquid waste recycling facility in Kelso, New South Wales.
The target, Echo Solve, is a contaminated waste treatment facility
located and operating principally in Altona, Victoria. Echo Solve
conducts contaminated soil treatment operations via thermal
desorption, drill mud disposal, hydro-excavation and soil washing.
The parties both supply contaminated waste treatment and
remediation services from their respective facilities.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition given:
a. there is no horizontal overlap between the parties in the
supply of contaminated waste treatment and remediation
services in Victoria
b. there are alternative suppliers of contaminated waste
treatment and remediation services in Victoria.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
